title: Scout holdout label resolution
description: One resolved label, as `scout holdout release` acts on it. Scout does not define a label file format of its own: it reads assay's saved `assay.label-packet-labels/v3`, joins each case through the private `assay.label-packet-key/v2` to a held evaluation and its frozen project, and resolves the pair to one of four labels and the action that label releases as. This schema records that resolution — what a reviewer's answer became, and on whose authority — so the mapping is reviewable without reading the implementation. It is the release-side companion to holdout-export.v1, which is what the reviewer was shown.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Bumped whenever a consumer must change to keep reading this.

holdout_id.description: The hold this label was applied to, as holdout-export.v1 reported it.

evaluation_id.description: The immutable source evaluation the key mapped this case to. It must match the hold's own source evaluation, and must belong to `project_key` as frozen on the hold; a mismatch is refused, never released on the recorded action instead.

project_key.description: The frozen project the decision was made against. Release never re-routes to another project — a label written for one project cannot grade a decision made for another.

case_id.description: The packet case id the label and the key both carry. Duplicated case ids, in either file, are refused.

label.description: The resolved label. See $defs.resolution for how a v3 case becomes one of these.

needs_thread.description: The reviewer's needs_thread answer, recorded as given. It does not enter the action mapping: the four labels above are the whole action vocabulary.

released_action.description: What the label releases as. exclusion→drop, in_post→respond, pointer→review, none→drop. A drop stops before generation; respond and review go through the ordinary reply-draft and critic path with every downstream gate intact.

authority.description: Who decided. `label` for a graded case; an ungraded hold releases under `recorded_action` instead and produces no record of this shape.

packet.description: The packet name the labels were saved against, which must equal the key's `name`.

packet_digest.description: The packet digest, which must be identical across the labels, the key, and the blind packet when it is supplied.

plan_digest.description: The plan digest, verified across the same files.

saved_at.description: When the reviewer saved the labels. Recorded on the hold as its labelled_at.

resolution.title: How one assay.label-packet-labels/v3 case resolves
resolution.description: Precedence, first match wins. 1. `exclusion` is anything other than the empty string or the literal "none", compared stripped and case-folded: an exclusion fired, and the label is `exclusion`. 2. `substance` is "in_post": the label is `in_post`. 3. `substance` is "pointer": the label is `pointer`. 4. `substance` is "none": the label is `none`. Anything else is refused. In particular a null `substance` with no exclusion is an incomplete answer, not a `none` — the reviewer was asked what the post carries and did not say — and an unrecognised `substance` value never falls back to a label that happens to be safe.
